evals.name: search-fetch-plot-cite
evals.prompt: Find Our World in Data's chart on the share of the population living in extreme poverty and plot India, Nigeria and China since 1990. Save the figure as poverty.png and tell me what to write under it as the source.
evals.expected_output: A line chart of the three countries from 1990 built from the chart's CSV, a short reading of the trend, and a source line that names the original data producer (World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform) and links to the OWID chart.
assertions: The chart was found through /api/search rather than a guessed slug, and the chosen chart's title is stated
The .csv request used csvType=filtered with an explicit country= filter for the three countries and a time= filter starting in 1990
The source line names the original producer from citationShort, not only 'Our World in Data', and includes the chart URL
The poverty line definition (the international poverty line and its dollar value) from the metadata is mentioned, since it is what 'extreme poverty' means in this chart

evals.name: fact-check-with-definition-mismatch
evals.prompt: A newsletter says: 'In Somalia one in five children dies before their fifth birthday.' Check this against Our World in Data and tell me whether it holds up.
evals.expected_output: The latest child mortality value for Somalia from OWID's child mortality chart, given with its unit (share or deaths per 100 live births) and year, compared to the 20% implied by 'one in five', a verdict on the claim, and the original source (UN IGME) with the chart link.
assertions: The value reported is for Somalia specifically, from the filtered CSV, with its year stated
The unit is stated correctly (share of children dying before age five, not a count), and 'one in five' is translated to 20% for the comparison
The verdict says whether the claim is consistent, outdated (true for an earlier year) or wrong, rather than forcing a yes/no
The original data producer is named from the metadata and the chart URL is given
If the metadata timespan does not reach the current year, the answer says which year the latest value is for instead of presenting it as current

evals.name: per-capita-join
evals.prompt: I have plastic-waste.csv with mismanaged plastic waste in tonnes for 2019, keyed by ISO3 code. Convert it to kilograms per person using Our World in Data population figures and give me the ranking.
evals.expected_output: A per-capita ranking in kg/person for all 12 countries, joined on ISO3 and the year 2019, with the population chart named and both sources cited.
assertions: The join used ISO3 codes and the year 2019, not country names
All 12 input countries appear in the output, or any that dropped out are named
The unit conversion from tonnes to kilograms was applied (factor of 1000)
The OWID population chart used is named or linked, and its producer is cited
The population CSV was requested with csvType=filtered and an explicit country= list, not the chart's default selection
